title: Erdős #396 OQ-04 → OQ-01 → OQ-01 → OQ-02 → OQ-02 → OQ-02 → OQ-01 → OQ-01: The Sharp Catalan Asymptotic Cₙ ∼ 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2})
description: Two long sub-threads of #396 had separately pinned the two halves of the growth of the Catalan numbers Cₙ: the exponent thread proved, from the recurrence alone, that the normalised sequence Cₙ/4ⁿ carries the critical exponent 3/2 (Cₙ/4ⁿ ∼ n^{−3/2}), the Catalan analogue of the central binomial's 1/2; the constant thread (parent entry) pinned the exact leading constant of the central binomial coefficient, C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π. This entry fuses the two into the single sharp statement for the Catalan numbers themselves: Cₙ·n·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π, i.e. Cₙ ∼ 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2}). Here n·√n is the square-root-free spelling of n^{3/2}; the extra factor of n over the central binomial's √n is exactly the 1/(n+1) of the Catalan normalisation (n+1)·Cₙ = C(2n,n), and it is what turns the 1/2 exponent into 3/2 while leaving the Wallis constant 1/√π unchanged. The central-binomial limit is reproved self-contained through Mathlib's Stirling sequence via the square-root-free bridge identity C(2n,n)²·n/16ⁿ = stirlingSeq(2n)²/stirlingSeq(n)⁴; the Catalan step is then the purely algebraic factorisation Cₙ·n·√n/4ⁿ = (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ)·(n/(n+1)) combined with n/(n+1) → 1.

overview.historicalContext: The #396 Catalan/central-binomial thread reads the two-term recurrence as a multiplicative step and tracks its deficit below the limiting rate 4. The exponent sub-thread extracted the critical exponents from the recurrence alone, with no Stirling input: Cₙ/4ⁿ ≤ exp(−(3/2)(H_{n+1}−1)) ∼ n^{−3/2} for the Catalan numbers, and C(2n,n)/4ⁿ ∼ n^{−1/2} for the central binomial coefficient, the difference of exactly 1 in the exponent being the n+1 factor of (n+1)·Cₙ = C(2n,n). The constant sub-thread then pinned the exact leading constant of the central binomial coefficient: the elementary squared-recurrence induction bracketed it in [1/2, 1/√3] (equivalently 3 ≤ π ≤ 4), and the parent entry closed the bracket to the single exact point 1/√π using Mathlib's Stirling limit. What remained was to combine the two — the proven 3/2 exponent and the proven 1/√π constant — into one sharp asymptotic for the Catalan numbers themselves.
overview.problemStatement: Does the doubly-normalised Catalan sequence Cₙ·n^{3/2}/4ⁿ converge, and to what exact constant? The exponent thread fixed the power n^{3/2} but said nothing about the constant; the constant thread fixed 1/√π but only for the central binomial coefficient C(2n,n) = (n+1)·Cₙ. Can the two be fused into a fully machine-checked proof that Cₙ ∼ 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2})?
overview.text: The limit is the exact Wallis constant: Cₙ·n·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π, where n·√n is the square-root-free spelling of n^{3/2}. The proof transports the central-binomial limit C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π across the elementary identity (n+1)·Cₙ = C(2n,n) (succ_mul_catalan_eq_centralBinom). Factoring Cₙ = C(2n,n)/(n+1) gives the exact algebraic decomposition Cₙ·(n·√n)/4ⁿ = (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ)·(n/(n+1)): the extra factor of n over the central binomial's √n splits as √n·n, and the n/(n+1) is precisely the Catalan weight. Since n/(n+1) → 1 (div_succ_tendsto_one, from n/(n+1) = 1 − 1/(n+1) and tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat), Filter.Tendsto.mul multiplies the two limits to 1/√π·1 = 1/√π, and Tendsto.congr' identifies the product sequence with the target on n ≥ 1 via field_simp. The central-binomial engine is reproved self-contained from Mathlib's Stirling limit through the square-root-free bridge identity C(2n,n)²·n/16ⁿ = stirlingSeq(2n)²/stirlingSeq(n)⁴.
overview.proofStrategy: Self-contained, import Mathlib only. (1) two_mul_factorial_eq: (2n)! = C(2n,n)·(n!·n!) over ℝ from Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial. (2) cb_sq_identity (the bridge, n ≥ 1): closed forms for stirlingSeq(n)⁴ and stirlingSeq(2n)² in which squaring kills every √ ((√(2n))⁴ = (2n)², (√(4n))² = 4n), then field_simp. (3) centralBinom_mul_sqrt_div_tendsto: compose tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi with n ↦ 2n, apply Tendsto.pow / Tendsto.div to get the ratio → π/π² = 1/π, transfer to (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ)² via Tendsto.congr' and cb_sq_identity, then Filter.Tendsto.sqrt with Real.sqrt_sq and √(1/π) = 1/√π. (4) div_succ_tendsto_one: n/(n+1) = 1 − 1/(n+1) → 1 − 0 = 1 via tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat and Tendsto.congr (field_simp; ring). (5) catalan_mul_pow_sqrt_div_tendsto (main): multiply the central-binomial limit by div_succ_tendsto_one (limit 1/√π·1 = 1/√π), then Tendsto.congr' on n ≥ 1 — rewrite C(2n,n) = (n+1)·Cₙ (exact_mod_cast succ_mul_catalan_eq_centralBinom) and close the algebraic identity (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ)·(n/(n+1)) = Cₙ·(n·√n)/4ⁿ with field_simp. (6) catalan_mul_sqrt_pi_div_tendsto_one: multiply by √π and simplify √π·(1/√π) = 1 (equivalent normalisation Cₙ·√π·n^{3/2}/4ⁿ → 1). (7) catalan_constant_eq_centralBinom_constant: package the Catalan and central-binomial limits side by side, both → 1/√π, exhibiting that the Catalan numbers inherit the Wallis constant unchanged.
keyInsights: **The exponent and the constant come from two different inputs, and they multiply cleanly.** The 3/2 exponent is a recurrence fact (it follows from the harmonic divergence of the per-step deficit, no analytic constant needed); the 1/√π constant is an analytic fact (the Wallis product, packaged in Mathlib's Stirling limit). This entry shows they assemble by a single Tendsto.mul: (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ) carries the constant, (n/(n+1)) carries the exponent shift, and their product is the sharp Catalan asymptotic.

**The 1/2 ↦ 3/2 exponent jump is exactly the Catalan weight 1/(n+1).** Algebraically Cₙ·(n·√n)/4ⁿ = (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ)·(n/(n+1)): the central binomial's normalisation needs √n, the Catalan's needs n·√n = n^{3/2}, and the extra factor of n is n/(n+1) → 1. So the entire difference between the two critical exponents is the single bounded factor n/(n+1), which contributes nothing to the limiting constant.

**The Catalan numbers inherit the Wallis constant unchanged.** Both Cₙ·n^{3/2}/4ⁿ and C(2n,n)·n^{1/2}/4ⁿ converge to the same 1/√π. Despite the different normalising powers, the constant is identical because n/(n+1) → 1 contributes a factor of exactly 1 — a fact made explicit by the side-by-side theorem catalan_constant_eq_centralBinom_constant.

**Square-and-reduce, reused.** The central-binomial engine is the same square-root-free device as the parent: square the target asymptotic (work with C(2n,n)²·n/16ⁿ) so every √ inside the Stirling sequence appears to an even power and the bridge identity becomes a polynomial closed by field_simp. Only one √ — the √n on the target — is restored, at the very end, by Filter.Tendsto.sqrt.

**A capstone fusing both #396 sub-threads.** The recurrence-only entries deliberately avoided Stirling to expose the exponents from harmonic divergence; pinning the constant genuinely requires the Wallis product. This entry isolates that single analytic input and shows the proven exponent and the proven constant combine into the classical sharp asymptotic Cₙ ∼ 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2}) with no further estimate.
prerequisites: The parent's central-binomial limit C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π, reproved here from Mathlib's Stirling sequence Stirling.tendsto_stirlingSeq_sqrt_pi
The Catalan–central-binomial identity Nat.succ_mul_catalan_eq_centralBinom : (n+1)·catalan n = centralBinom n

conclusion.summary: The doubly-normalised Catalan sequence converges to the exact Wallis constant: Cₙ·n·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π, equivalently Cₙ ∼ 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2}). The proof transports the central-binomial limit C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ → 1/√π across the elementary identity (n+1)·Cₙ = C(2n,n): the exact factorisation Cₙ·(n·√n)/4ⁿ = (C(2n,n)·√n/4ⁿ)·(n/(n+1)) combines the proven Wallis constant with the bounded weight n/(n+1) → 1, whose product is the sharp asymptotic. The central-binomial engine is reproved self-contained from Mathlib's Stirling limit via the square-root-free bridge C(2n,n)²·n/16ⁿ = stirlingSeq(2n)²/stirlingSeq(n)⁴. All seven theorems are fully machine-checked with no axioms or sorries.
conclusion.implications: The entry fuses the two #396 sub-threads — the recurrence-derived 3/2 exponent and the Stirling-derived 1/√π constant — into the single classical sharp asymptotic for the Catalan numbers, with the 1/2 ↦ 3/2 exponent jump isolated as the bounded factor n/(n+1). It makes explicit that the Catalan numbers inherit the central binomial's Wallis constant unchanged. The factor-and-multiply method is reusable: any asymptotic of the form aₙ·wₙ where wₙ → 1 is a bounded reweighting (here the Catalan-to-central-binomial weight n/(n+1)) inherits the leading constant of aₙ verbatim.
openQuestions: The convergence is first-order: Cₙ·n^{3/2}/4ⁿ → 1/√π. Can the same factor-and-multiply device, applied to a second-order central-binomial expansion C(2n,n) = (4ⁿ/√(πn))(1 − 1/(8n) + O(1/n²)), produce a verified second-order Catalan expansion Cₙ = (4ⁿ/(√π n^{3/2}))(1 − 9/(8n) + O(1/n²)), where the −9/(8n) is the sum of the central binomial's −1/(8n) and the −1/(n+1) ≈ −1/n of the Catalan weight expanded to second order?

The weight n/(n+1) → 1 contributes 1 to the limit but a −1/n correction at next order. Is there a clean recurrence-level statement — analogous to the harmonic-deficit description of the exponent — that captures the full Catalan-to-central-binomial weight (n/(n+1)) and its asymptotic expansion, closing the loop between the recurrence-only thread and the Stirling-based constant?

Ancestor OQ: the 3/2 critical exponent of Catalan growth from the recurrence, Cₙ/4ⁿ ∼ n^{−3/2}, proved without Stirling. This entry supplies the exact constant of that asymptotic, Cₙ ∼ 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2}).
Root problem. The Catalan numbers Cₙ = C(2n,n)/(n+1) are a central object whose exact growth rate 4ⁿ/(√π·n^{3/2}) is established here.
